correctness.rationale: For each G-edge e=uv, closed neighborhood in line graph is S_u∪S_v; clique complex Y is union of star simplices because triangle-free. Any face outside Y contains two disjoint G-edges a,b. Every center must join an endpoint of a to an endpoint of b; triangle-free implies at most two such connectors; two only if the face is an opposite-edge pair of a unique four-cycle. Retain all tetrahedral boundaries B_C on E(C). Every remaining face has unique center e and pairs with face toggling e; descending lower-face cardinality proves each pair a genuine elementary free-face collapse, independent of overlapping squares. Star-simplex nerve is G; splitting each B_C into two triangular disks with distinct interior diagonals yields one square-completion 2-cell and one additional S2. Hence K~Q(G)∨qS2, H1=H1(G)/<four-cycle classes>, H2=H2(Q)⊕Z^q, higher homology 0. Independently constructed K, retained T and executed all claimed free-face collapses on K2,3, K3,3 and C6, including all their overlapping 4-cycles; finite checks supplement general symbolic center proof.
residual_risks: Connected finite simple triangle-free G with at least one edge; triangles destroy center uniqueness. Q(G) may retain nontrivial H1 or torsion; do not claim purely wedge of spheres generally.

originality.rationale: Previously published girth>=5 theorem gives K=N[L(G)] collapses to Y=Cl(L(G)), but explicitly excludes four-cycles. The new exact relative collapse handles every finite connected triangle-free G, including arbitrarily overlapping four-cycles, and adds each tetrahedral boundary B_C; its homotopy splitting is Q(G) plus one S2 per four-cycle, even for K2,3. The known Y≃G and general graph Čech neighborhood formulas are acknowledged. A separate published square-completion theorem concerns the Čech nerve of G itself under additional no-K2,3 restriction, not L(G) with triangles, so does not imply this result directly. Best-of-knowledge novelty PASS, with residual equivalent nerve-model risk.
residual_risks: A different older square-filling or closed-neighborhood construction could be equivalent under a nonobvious functor; published SCOPE square-completion counterpart not wholly reread this run.
The homotopy split is not a literal simplicial collapse to a wedge; formula keeps Q(G) possibly with torsion in first homology.

value.rationale: The theorem is a sharp structural extension from girth-five to all triangle-free graphs with unrestricted square overlap. It supplies an explicit simple-homotopy reduction and a computable homotopy and integral homology description via graph square completion; K2,3 and K3,3 illustrate nontrivial new phenomena outside earlier no-square/no-K2,3 hypotheses.
residual_risks: Does not classify homotopy of Q(G) for every graph or higher filtration scales; useful because reduction to Q(G) is already complete and natural.

final_claim: For every finite connected simple triangle-free graph G with an edge, N[L(G)] simplicially collapses to Cl(L(G)) united with tetrahedral boundaries B_C indexed by all four-cycles C, and N[L(G)] ≃ Q(G) ∨ wedge^{q} S² where Q(G) attaches one square 2-cell per 4-cycle; H1 quotient and H2 splitting follow integrally without restrictions on square overlap.
limitations: Assumes triangle-free finite connected simple G; homotopy formula uses square-completion Q(G) rather than fully classifying its homotopy.
Published related square-completion theorem for other graph nerve not wholly reread this run; equivalent constructions remain priority risk.
